messages:
maya: Heads-up — hitting a weird state with the Python async client and env var key rotation. Two short repros below.

maya: Setup: 2 clients in the same process (service level):
```py
client_a = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY_A'))
client_b = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY_B'))
# both are long-lived, used across requests
```

maya: Problem 1: rotate REDWOOD_KEY_A at runtime, client_a starts returning 401s for a few seconds while client_b still works. After ~10s it recovers without any explicit refresh call.

maya: Problem 2: if you create a new async client after rotation (e.g. ephemeral per-request), sometimes the new client picks up the old key for a request or two. Observed with aiohttp-based transport.

maya: Minimal log excerpt (sanitized):
```
2025-11-03T14:02:10Z maya request id=aa11 auth=keyA -> 401
2025-11-03T14:02:12Z maya request id=aa12 auth=keyA -> 401
2025-11-03T14:02:15Z maya request id=aa13 auth=keyA -> 200 (recovered)
2025-11-03T14:02:16Z maya request id=bb01 auth=keyB -> 200
2025-11-03T14:02:17Z maya request id=cc01 auth=keyA (new client) -> 401
2025-11-03T14:02:18Z maya request id=cc02 auth=keyA (new client) -> 200
```
```

maya: hypothesis: there's a shared auth cache or module-level provider that races during env updates, plus the async connector reuses a session with stale headers.

maya: Repro script attached (short): rapidly flip env var and create clients in parallel tasks. Happy to paste if useful.

jake: ugh, thanks for the detailed repro. can you confirm whether you're using the latest 0.11.x py-sdk? we had an env-binding change there.

maya: yup 0.11.4. also happens on 0.11.3 in prod. i didn't try 0.12 alpha.

anna: tagging infra — @ops-bot can you check if any recent deploy touched auth provider code? :eyes:

ops-bot: deploys since 2025-10-30 touching auth/ -> 2025-11-01 03:12 UTC (PR #3421) — contained header propagation tweaks.

sam: quick question — are you using our credential-provider callback or passing raw api_key strings?

maya: raw strings from env (os.getenv) at client construction time. not using callback.

jake: two probable causes from experience: 1) module-level cached header dict updated asynchronously and shared across clients, 2) aiohttp ClientSession getting default headers at creation and reused in a pool while env rotates.

jake: we should make client construction always read creds from a per-instance provider and avoid any global header mutation. also ensure async client recreates session headers when cred list changes.

anna: short-term mitigation: rotate keys via a central provider that updates clients via an explicit `client.update_credentials(new_key)` API. longer term, SDK should detect env var rotation if callback registered.

maya: agree. can we please get a small fix/PR that ensures headers are not mutated globally? i can prototype.

jake: please do — couple points: keep it opt-in to avoid perf regression for tiny apps. also add a unit test that simulates concurrent client creation + env flip.

maya: will open a draft PR with tests. also i'll include a small async repro script in the repo under examples/ that demonstrates the race.

sam: also adding a feature request: credential-provider interface that supports hot-reload + async refresh hook. put in issue tracker?

maya: filed ISSUE-DEVEX-891: "py-sdk: credential provider interface + hot-reload for async clients" with reproduction and logs.

jake: nice. assigning to eng-ml/sdks. thanks for the repro, maya — this one annoyed me in an integration test last week. :+1:

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for auth/ header-fix branch next week.

maya: awesome — will follow the PR. if anyone needs the repro snippets DM me.

anna: thx — marking this thread for triage in Monday SDK sync. :white_check_mark:
